suggestions.assertion: No content is copied verbatim from the source beyond a short quoted phrase
suggestions.reason: As currently satisfied by the skill's own mandatory Step 5 gate, this assertion is effectively 'check_verbatim_overlap.py exits 0 at its default 15-word threshold.' That gate has a real blind spot: my independent --threshold 10 pass on this very run found several 10-14-word narrative clauses reproduced almost word-for-word from the source, immediately below the cutoff. A run that trims every flagged run down to exactly 14 words would pass the gate while still being substantially unparaphrased. Consider grading this assertion against a lower threshold (e.g. 10-12 words) or requiring a manual spot-check step in addition to the mechanical script, rather than treating the 15-word script's exit code as sufficient on its own.

quick_validate.py hard-requires the containing directory's name to equal the skill's `name` field. Any eval run that delivers output flat into a directory literally named `outputs/` (as this eval's own harness does, per its task instructions) will fail this check for a reason that has nothing to do with the skill's actual quality. This eval either needs its harness to deliver output into a correctly-named subfolder before this assertion is graded, or the assertion needs to explicitly account for the naming mismatch the way the grading task's methodology note already does for the references/ question — otherwise every future with_skill run under this harness will spuriously fail this assertion regardless of output quality.

eval_feedback.overall: 6 of 7 expectations pass, with strong independent (not transcript-trusting) verification on every one: the mandatory mechanical verbatim check, the advisory lint, and the structural validator were all re-run by hand rather than taken on faith, and several precise numeric claims in the transcript (character counts, token counts, description length) were independently reproduced and matched exactly, which is a good sign of a transcript that isn't fabricating specifics. The one failure is substantive, not a technicality: real near-verbatim narrative-clause copying survived the fix pass, just below the mechanical script's default threshold, which is exactly the class of problem this eval was re-run to catch. The two eval-feedback suggestions above target the two assertions whose current operationalization (a single script's default threshold; a hard directory-name-match check against a harness that can't satisfy it) can produce a false result independent of actual skill quality.
